items.titulo: New study maps the genetic landscape of bovine TB across Wales
items.resumen: Bovine tuberculosis is evolving in different ways across different regions in Wales, according to the most detailed analysis of the bacterium conducted to date. One of the most significant animal health challenges facing Wales, bovine TB affects cattle health and farm businesses and places considerable emotional, social and financial pressures on farming communities.

items.titulo: Independent technique validates landmark M87* image
items.resumen: The 2019 Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) image was the work of hundreds of scientists and captured the first direct view of a black hole's shadow—becoming one of the most recognized scientific images of the modern era. A team of four from CSIRO, Australia's national science agency, has developed a powerful new imaging technique that validated the landmark 2019 image of the black hole at the center of galaxy M87.

items.titulo: Tumours survive a stalled respiratory chain by draining surplus NADH. Plug the drain and metformin turns lethal

Working in human cancer lines, researchers describe a mitochondrial-cytosolic circuit built on pyruvate carboxylase, malate dehydrogenases 1 and 2, and malic enzyme 1 that converts NADH from both compartments into cytosolic NADPH. They have found that carefully controlled microscopic cracks can enhance the performance of an antibacterial coating, which helps destroy dangerous bacteria when activated with a small electrical charge.

items.titulo: New study explains why we may feel the cold more as we age
items.resumen: Most of us expect to become more sensitive to cold as we get older. Unlike white fat, which primarily stores energy, thermogenic fat is a special type of body fat that burns calories to produce heat and helps us stay warm.
